extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled by collecting 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA) and creating 3 new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). Existing MathQA datasets were limited to 400 examples each. VQA datasets were filtered using heuristic rules for numeric answers or quantity words, then manually labeled by three expert annotators using majority voting. New datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields with a two-step review process ensuring 99.2% inter-annotation consistency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (including Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA, ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS) and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by manual labeling. Discrepancies in annotations were resolved through discussion among the review team.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples from VQA datasets that likely involve mathematical reasoning based on numeric answers or quantity words. Manual labeling by expert annotators was performed to determine if examples involve mathematical reasoning. Metadata such as question type, answer type, task category, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills were annotated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. A two-step process was employed: initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team to ensure consensus. For mathematical reasoning categories, expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples to verify automatic annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2% for the newly collected 736 questions, with only 6 disagreements. Fleiss Kappa score for labeling mathematical reasoning among three annotators was 0.775, indicating substantial consistency.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; expert annotators; human annotators with a high school diploma or higher for human performance baseline.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used for answer extraction with >99.5% accuracy)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples). Answer labels for the test set are not publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform is maintained. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process, with commitments to maintain datasets, refine data noise, and evolve the leaderboard in response to community feedback.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate research progress of LLMs and LMMs. It highlights the critical role of such benchmarks in developing general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset covers diverse visual contexts and mathematical skills but may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The focus on specific domains like science and college-level math makes data collection labor-intensive, potentially limiting scalability and generalizability to other domains.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to sourcing from original data providers, leading to heterogeneous annotation formats. The benchmark's focus on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts limits its generalizability to other domains. It focuses exclusively on recent and prominent models, and future iterations aim to encompass broader problems and visual contexts with unified annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is used for comprehensive, quantitative evaluation of foundation models' mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts, including zero-shot and few-shot settings, and tool-augmented prompting.
